excerpt_i18n.en: In the past, reviewing highlight moments from football matches required editors to sift through footage, find goals, celebrations, slow-motion replays, and audience reactions, then cut, package, add subtitles, and finally distribute to different platforms. The process was lengthy and labor-intensive, and capturing traffic from trending moments depended entirely on human experience and reaction speed. Now, this workflow has been broken down and reassembled, with models and toolchains taking over the entire production pipeline for sports highlight videos. In this new chain, AI can already understand live streams in real time, recognize signals such as camera switches, audio changes, player celebrations, and referee whistles, quickly return highlight clips after key events, and generate ready-to-distribute standalone segments. By the time a trending moment erupts, the video is already ready. The underlying change is not just that a specific tool has become more efficient; it is that the production of audio and video content is evolving from a human-driven workflow to an agent-driven workflow. This is not just about using models to generate and process audio and video content, but also about forming new production tools and new production processes on this basis, truly approaching the ideal state of "one sentence to create a finished video." This paradigm shift in video production requires support from a new technical foundation. Hang Mengyu, product lead for the Volcano Engine AI Media Platform, mentioned at the Intelligent Video Cloud sub-forum of the 2026 Summer FORCE Conference that moving from "generating a segment of footage" to "delivering a finished video that can go live, be consumed, and be distributed to audiences" still requires a full set of professional audio and video processing work.

Leiphone has learned that on June 30, the "2026 XBOT General-Purpose Catering Embodied Robot Launch" was held in Beijing by Yingzhi XBOT. Key milestones include product, platform, commercial closed loop, and ecosystem openness. The company officially released its self-developed embodied operating system XOS 3.0, the AI Agent product "Aibao Shop Manager," and three new general-purpose catering embodied robots covering coffee, ice cream, and full-service scenarios. Together, they form a complete "one brain, multiple forms" intelligent system.

XOS 3.0: An embodied operating system designed for "one brain, multiple forms." As the technical foundation behind Aibao Shop Manager, XOS 3.0 functions as the "operating system" for embodied intelligence. Based on this architecture, XOS 3.0 enables cross-embodiment skill transfer—operations learned once can be reused after changing robot morphology, truly achieving "one development, multiple forms reuse." This overcomes the key barriers of high scene migration costs and weak generalization that have long plagued the industry. Supporting this upgrade are three core capabilities of XOS 3.0: First, the VLA (Vision-Language-Action) architecture, which gives robots the full-chain ability to "see, understand, and execute." Second, a full-chain R&D closed loop covering algorithms, hardware, interaction, and productization, enabling rapid deployment of technical capabilities from lab to commercial scenarios. excerpt_i18n.es: Según información de Leiphone, el 30 de junio se celebró en Pekín el "Lanzamiento de XBOT 2026: Robots Embodiedos Universales para Restaurantes", donde se presentaron, como hitos clave de producto, plataforma, circuito cerrado comercial y ecosistema abierto, el sistema operativo embodiedo propio XOS 3.0, el producto AI Agent "AiBao Store Manager", y tres nuevos robots embodiedos universales para servicios de café, helados y cobertura completa.
